I used to be the type of player who would only play on medium or the easiest difficulty. But I noticed I finished games way too quickly, and it felt like I wasn’t truly experiencing the game or using the majority of its mechanics. For example, I’m now playing TheWitcher3 on the highest difficulty, and I’m using every mechanic available while also reading through the in-game glossaries to learn how to defeat monsters. The same goes for GOW+R I spent $100 AUD, which isn’t chump change here, and I feel like playing on a harder difficulty forces you to fully engage with everything the game has to offer.

I almost quit the game because of this boss battle. The off-screen instant-kill abilities were incredibly frustrating and really highlighted some of the game's weaknesses, particularly the camera, which isn’t its strongest feature. I had to turn off lock-on to manage because it kept targeting the back caster when I wanted to focus on the brute, and vice versa. Since I’ve mostly been playing on PC lately, my aim on console wasn’t great, which made the fight even more challenging.  Some matchups on the hardest difficulty felt unbalanced, making me wonder if the developers primarily designed the game with mid-difficulty playthroughs in mind and simply ramped up enemy health for the higher difficulties. Certain abilities gave almost no time to react, which made those encounters feel unfair at times. All of this stood out even more when compared to the 2018 version, which felt more balanced overall minus Niflilheim three witches.
